```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Beredaki 2024 used an in vitro dialysis/diffusion pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic
model to study micafungin against *Candida parapsilosis*. Conventional PK/PD
targets (stasis, 50% of maximal effect) give a low probability of target
attainment (PTA) for isolates the clinical breakpoint calls susceptible, even
though echinocandins work well clinically against this species. The paper
proposes a new target, the exposure giving 10% of the maximal effect at a low
starting inoculum (EI10 = 28 tAUC0-24/MIC), which restores PTA >= 95% for
susceptible isolates at the standard 100 mg daily dose.

The paper fitted four independent exposure-response curves -- two media (RPMI
with and without 10% pooled human serum) by two starting inocula (10^4 and
10^3 CFU/mL) -- so the extraction is four model files sharing this vignette:

* 10% serum, 10^4 CFU/mL: `Beredaki_2024_micafungin_serum_inoc1e4`
* 10% serum, 10^3 CFU/mL: `Beredaki_2024_micafungin_serum_inoc1e3`
* serum-free RPMI, 10^4 CFU/mL: `Beredaki_2024_micafungin_rpmi_inoc1e4`
* serum-free RPMI, 10^3 CFU/mL: `Beredaki_2024_micafungin_rpmi_inoc1e3`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkad360>

```{r load-models}
model_names <- c(
  serum_1e4 = "Beredaki_2024_micafungin_serum_inoc1e4",
  serum_1e3 = "Beredaki_2024_micafungin_serum_inoc1e3",
  rpmi_1e4 = "Beredaki_2024_micafungin_rpmi_inoc1e4",
  rpmi_1e3 = "Beredaki_2024_micafungin_rpmi_inoc1e3"
)
mods <- lapply(model_names, function(nm) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(nm)))
# Named population-parameter vectors, used to evaluate the exposure-response
# curves directly from each model's ini().
thetas <- lapply(mods, function(m) m$theta)
```

```{r citation, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("* Citation: ", mods$serum_1e3$reference, "\n", sep = "")
```

```{r description, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("* Description (10% serum, 10^3 CFU/mL): ", mods$serum_1e3$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

# Population

Three echinocandin-susceptible *C. parapsilosis sensu stricto* clinical isolates
were tested -- CP639, CP795 and CP732, with identical EUCAST and CLSI micafungin
MICs of 2, 1 and 0.5 mg/L -- together with a pan-echinocandin-resistant isolate
(*fks1* F652S plus the natural P660A polymorphism, MIC > 8 mg/L) against which no
effect was seen at any exposure. In 10% human serum CP732 did not grow, so the
serum curves rest on CP639 and CP795.

The dynamic model is an external compartment (a conical flask on a peristaltic
pump) connected to an internal compartment: a 10 mL semipermeable cellulose
dialysis tube (300 kDa cut-off) inoculated at 10^4 or 10^3 CFU/mL. The medium
was RPMI 1640 buffered with MOPS to pH 7.0, with or without 10% heat-inactivated
pooled human serum. Micafungin was added once daily for 72 h at free peak
concentrations of 0.5, 1.8 and 4 mg/L in RPMI (Figure 2) and total peak
concentrations of 2, 8, 32 and 64 mg/L with serum (Figure 3). The fungal load
was sampled at 0, 4, 8, 24, 48 and 72 h (limit of detection 10 CFU/mL).

The same information is available programmatically via each model's
`population` metadata, e.g.
`readModelDb("Beredaki_2024_micafungin_serum_inoc1e3")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry. The table below collects them in one place.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `d/dt(central) <- -kel * central`; `Cc <- central / vc` | n/a | Methods, "In vitro PK": drug added at the target Cmax once daily, mono-exponential decay with a target half-life; Figure 1 |
| `lkel` (serum) | `log(log(2) / 11)` | Results, "In vitro PK": achieved t1/2 11 (7-18) h in RPMI + 10% serum |
| `lkel` (RPMI) | `log(log(2) / 8)` | Results, "In vitro PK": achieved t1/2 8 (6-11) h in RPMI |
| `lvc` | `log(0.010)` (fixed) | Methods, "In vitro PK/PD model": 10 mL internal compartment |
| `tau` | 24 h (fixed) | Methods: drug added once daily; the index is AUC0-24/MIC |
| `cmax` | 32 mg/L (serum) / 1.8 mg/L (RPMI) (fixed, design) | Figure 3 legend (tCmax 2, 8, 32, 64 mg/L) / Figure 2 legend (fCmax 0.5, 1.8, 4 mg/L) |
| `change72 <- e0 - (e0 - emax) * ei^hill / (ei^hill + ec50^hill)` | n/a | Methods, "PK/PD analysis": `E = (Emax - Emin) * EI^n / (EI^n + EI50^n) + Emin` |
| `e0` (Emin) | 4 / 5.23 (serum 10^4 / 10^3) | Results, "PK/PD analysis": "the Emin (4 versus 5.23)" |
| `e0` (Emin) | 3.78 / 4.40 (RPMI 10^4 / 10^3) | **digitised** from Figure 4, right panel |
| `emax` | -3 / -2 (10^4 / 10^3) (fixed) | Methods, "PK/PD analysis": Emax constrained to -3 (10^4) and -2 (10^3) log10 CFU/mL |
| `lec50` (EI50) | `log(240)` / `log(124)` tAUC0-24/MIC (serum 10^4 / 10^3) | Table 1 and Results, "PK/PD analysis" |
| `lec50` (EI50) | `log(25.1)` / `log(41.3)` fAUC0-24/MIC (RPMI 10^4 / 10^3) | **digitised** from Figure 4, right panel (Table 1: 27 / 46) |
| `lhill` (n) | `log(2.9)` (serum 10^4) | Results, "PK/PD analysis": n = -2.9 (falling-curve sign convention) |
| `lhill` (n) | `log(1.45)` (serum 10^3) | Table 1 targets and Figure 4; Results print -1.15 -- see Assumptions and deviations |
| `lhill` (n) | `log(2.56)` / `log(4.82)` (RPMI 10^4 / 10^3) | **digitised** from Figure 4, right panel |
| `mic` | 2 mg/L (fixed) | Methods, "Candida isolates": CP639 EUCAST/CLSI MIC 2 mg/L |
| `log10_cfu0` | 4.28 / 3.2 (serum), 3.94 / 3.06 (RPMI) (fixed) | Results, "In vitro PD": measured mean t = 0 densities of the drug-free controls |
| `d/dt(bact) <- log(10) * (change72 / 72) * bact` | n/a | Methods, "In vitro PD": effect assessed as the log10 CFU/mL change at 72 h vs the start of therapy |
| `propSd`, `addSd_log10cfu` | 0 (fixed) | Not reported; only R^2 (>= 0.90 with serum, >= 0.77 without) |

Reference PK/PD targets (Beredaki 2024 Table 1, mean with 95% CI). The serum
curves are indexed on total AUC (tAUC0-24/MIC); the serum-free curves on the
AUC in protein-free medium, i.e. fAUC0-24/MIC. The paper converts between the
two with 99.75% protein binding (fAUC = 0.0025 x tAUC).

| Medium | Inoculum | Index | Stasis | EI50 | EI10 | EI5 |
|--------|----------|-------|--------|------|------|-----|
| RPMI | 10^4 | fAUC/MIC | 28 (19-46) | 27 (18-39) | 10 (5-24) | 9 (3-21) |
| RPMI | 10^3 | fAUC/MIC | 50 (42-65) | 46 (38-56) | 27 (18-41) | 22 (13-39) |
| RPMI + 10% serum | 10^4 | tAUC/MIC | 272 (198-380) | 240 (180-320) | 113 (48-260) | 87 (30-249) |
| RPMI + 10% serum | 10^3 | tAUC/MIC | 240 (176-352) | 124 (88-184) | 28 (16-64) | 16 (8-48) |

# Virtual cohort

The in vitro experiment has no virtual population: each arm is one dialysis tube
with a defined isolate (fixing `mic`) and a defined target peak concentration
(fixing `cmax`). Arms are enumerated deterministically and every simulation
below is a typical-value solve; the models carry no between-subject variability,
matching a paper that reports none.

```{r helpers}
# Beredaki 2024 re-spiked the internal compartment to the target peak once daily
# (Figure 1: the target peaks are identical at 0, 24 and 48 h). The first dose
# raises the empty compartment to `cmax`; each later dose tops up the fraction
# lost over the preceding interval.
make_events <- function(cmax, kel, vc = 0.010, tau = 24, tmax = 72, dt = 0.25) {
  first_amt <- cmax * vc
  topup_amt <- cmax * (1 - exp(-kel * tau)) * vc
  dose_times <- seq(0, tmax - tau, by = tau)
  doses <- data.frame(
    time = dose_times,
    amt = c(first_amt, rep(topup_amt, length(dose_times) - 1L)),
    cmt = "central", evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  # Observation rows sit on the ODE state `central`; `dvid = 1L` selects the Cc
  # endpoint. rxode2 returns every algebraic observable (Cc, ei, change72,
  # log10cfu) as a column at these rows.
  obs <- data.frame(
    time = seq(0, tmax, by = dt),
    amt = NA_real_, cmt = "central", evid = 0L, dvid = 1L
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |> dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

# One deterministic arm. `kel` defaults to the model's own achieved half-life.
solve_arm <- function(mod, cmax, mic = 2, kel = NULL, ...) {
  if (is.null(kel)) kel <- exp(mod$theta[["lkel"]])
  ev <- make_events(cmax = cmax, kel = kel, ...)
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod, ev,
    params = c(cmax = cmax, mic = mic, lkel = log(kel)),
    useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cmax_nominal = cmax, mic_nominal = mic, thalf_nominal = log(2) / kel)
}
```

# Replicate Figure 1: in vitro pharmacokinetics

Figure 1 (bottom panels) shows the measured q24h micafungin profiles in the
internal compartment against the target human profile (half-life 15 h), in RPMI
(panel a) and in RPMI + 10% serum (panel b). The models carry the achieved
half-lives (8 h and 11 h); the target profiles are obtained by overriding
`lkel`.

```{r figure-1}
pk_spec <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,       ~panel,              ~cmax, ~label,
  "rpmi_1e4",   "(a) RPMI",            0.5, "fCmax 0.5 mg/L",
  "rpmi_1e4",   "(a) RPMI",            1.8, "fCmax 1.8 mg/L",
  "rpmi_1e4",   "(a) RPMI",            4.0, "fCmax 4 mg/L",
  "serum_1e4",  "(b) RPMI + 10% serum",  2, "tCmax 2 mg/L",
  "serum_1e4",  "(b) RPMI + 10% serum",  8, "tCmax 8 mg/L",
  "serum_1e4",  "(b) RPMI + 10% serum", 32, "tCmax 32 mg/L"
)

# Every arm at the achieved and at the target half-life, over `tmax` hours.
solve_pk_spec <- function(tmax) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pk_spec)), function(i) {
    s <- pk_spec[i, ]
    mod <- mods[[s$model]]
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      solve_arm(mod, cmax = s$cmax, tmax = tmax) |>
        dplyr::mutate(profile = "in vitro (achieved t1/2)"),
      solve_arm(mod, cmax = s$cmax, kel = log(2) / 15, tmax = tmax) |>
        dplyr::mutate(profile = "target (t1/2 15 h)")
    ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(panel = s$panel, label = s$label, arm = paste(s$label, "-", profile))
  }))
}

pk_arms <- solve_pk_spec(tmax = 72)

ggplot(pk_arms, aes(time, Cc, colour = label, linetype = profile)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 72, by = 12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Micafungin concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    title = "Figure 1 -- simulated q24h micafungin profiles in the internal compartment",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 (bottom panels) of Beredaki 2024."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis over the first dosing interval -- the window that
defines the paper's PK/PD index. Because the compartment is re-spiked at 24 h,
the 24 h observation of the multiple-dose profile above is the new peak, not the
trough; the NCA therefore uses a separate solve that stops at 24 h, which is
identical to the first interval of the q24h regimen. The arm is the treatment
grouping variable.

```{r pknca}
pk_first <- solve_pk_spec(tmax = 24)

sim_nca <- pk_first |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)

# Guarantee a time = 0 record per arm. The dose is a bolus spike, so the t = 0
# value is already the peak; the bind_rows/distinct pattern is a defensive no-op.
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, arm) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(arm, id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(arm, id, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id)

dose_df <- pk_first |>
  dplyr::distinct(arm, cmax_nominal) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = cmax_nominal * 0.010) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm)

dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 24,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tidy <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_tidy |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)" = auclast,
    "t1/2 (h)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PKNCA results for the simulated in vitro PK arms.")
```

## Comparison against published PK values

Beredaki 2024 specifies the target peak of every arm and reports the achieved
in vitro half-lives (8 h in RPMI, 11 h with serum) and the target human
half-life (15 h).

```{r nca-compare}
published_pk <- pk_first |>
  dplyr::distinct(arm, cmax = cmax_nominal, half.life = thalf_nominal)

cmp_pk <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_tidy,
  reference = published_pk,
  by = "arm",
  params = c("cmax", "half.life"),
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

knitr::kable(
  cmp_pk,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated vs published in vitro PK. Reference Cmax values are the target",
    "peak concentrations (Figures 1-3); reference half-lives are the achieved",
    "values from Results (8 h RPMI, 11 h serum) or the 15 h design target.",
    "* differs from reference by >20%."
  )
)
```

The PK/PD index inside each model is the closed form of the first-interval AUC,
`cmax * (1 - exp(-kel * tau)) / kel`. It must agree with the PKNCA AUC0-24 of
the simulated profile -- the strictest check that dose amounts, volume and
elimination are wired together correctly.

```{r nca-assert}
chk <- nca_tidy |>
  dplyr::left_join(published_pk, by = "arm", suffix = c("_sim", "_ref")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    pk_first |>
      dplyr::filter(time == 0) |>
      dplyr::mutate(auc_closed = dplyr::coalesce(tauc24, fauc24)) |>
      dplyr::distinct(arm, auc_closed),
    by = "arm"
  )
# Same drawn parameters on both sides, so these are numerical-error bounds.
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$cmax_sim / chk$cmax_ref - 1)) < 0.01)
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$half.life_sim / chk$half.life_ref - 1)) < 0.01)
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$auclast / chk$auc_closed - 1)) < 0.01)
```

# Replicate Figure 4: the exposure-response relationships

Figure 4 plots the 72 h change in log10 CFU/mL against fAUC0-24/MIC with 10%
serum (left, R^2 >= 0.90) and in RPMI (right, R^2 >= 0.77). The packaged models
reproduce the curves directly from `e0`, `emax`, `ec50` and `hill`; the serum
curves are drawn on the fAUC axis with the paper's 99.75% protein binding.

```{r figure-4}
fu <- 0.0025

# Exposure-response evaluated from a model's theta vector on the model's
# native index (tAUC/MIC for serum, fAUC/MIC for RPMI).
er_curve <- function(th, ei) {
  e0 <- th[["e0"]]
  emax <- th[["emax"]]
  ec50 <- exp(th[["lec50"]])
  hill <- exp(th[["lhill"]])
  e0 - (e0 - emax) * ei^hill / (ei^hill + ec50^hill)
}

curve_spec <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,      ~panel,              ~inoculum,     ~to_fauc,
  "serum_1e4", "RPMI + 10% serum", "10^4 CFU/mL",  fu,
  "serum_1e3", "RPMI + 10% serum", "10^3 CFU/mL",  fu,
  "rpmi_1e4",  "RPMI",             "10^4 CFU/mL",  1,
  "rpmi_1e3",  "RPMI",             "10^3 CFU/mL",  1
)

fauc_grid <- 10^seq(-2, 2, length.out = 400)
curves <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(curve_spec)), function(i) {
  s <- curve_spec[i, ]
  tibble::tibble(
    fauc_mic = fauc_grid,
    change = er_curve(thetas[[s$model]], fauc_grid / s$to_fauc),
    panel = s$panel, inoculum = s$inoculum
  )
}))

ggplot(curves, aes(fauc_mic, change, colour = inoculum)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("10^4 CFU/mL" = "black", "10^3 CFU/mL" = "grey60")) +
  labs(
    x = "micafungin fAUC0-24 / MIC", y = "72 h change in log10 CFU/mL",
    colour = "Starting inoculum",
    title = "Figure 4 -- in vitro exposure-response of micafungin",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Beredaki 2024. Dashed line = stasis."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Validation against the Table 1 PK/PD targets

Each packaged curve is inverted to recover the exposure index at stasis (no
change from the starting inoculum) and at 50%, 10% and 5% of the maximal effect,
where "x% of the maximal effect" is the exposure that moves the change x% of the
way from `e0` to `emax`.

```{r table-1}
invert_curve <- function(th, target_change) {
  stats::uniroot(
    function(lei) er_curve(th, exp(lei)) - target_change,
    interval = log(c(1e-4, 1e6)), tol = 1e-10
  )$root |> exp()
}

target_change <- function(th, endpoint) {
  e0 <- th[["e0"]]
  emax <- th[["emax"]]
  switch(endpoint,
    stasis = 0,
    EI50 = e0 - 0.50 * (e0 - emax),
    EI10 = e0 - 0.10 * (e0 - emax),
    EI5 = e0 - 0.05 * (e0 - emax)
  )
}

table1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,      ~index,      ~endpoint, ~reported, ~lo,   ~hi,
  "serum_1e4", "tAUC/MIC",  "stasis",  272,       198,   380,
  "serum_1e4", "tAUC/MIC",  "EI50",    240,       180,   320,
  "serum_1e4", "tAUC/MIC",  "EI10",    113,        48,   260,
  "serum_1e4", "tAUC/MIC",  "EI5",      87,        30,   249,
  "serum_1e3", "tAUC/MIC",  "stasis",  240,       176,   352,
  "serum_1e3", "tAUC/MIC",  "EI50",    124,        88,   184,
  "serum_1e3", "tAUC/MIC",  "EI10",     28,        16,    64,
  "serum_1e3", "tAUC/MIC",  "EI5",      16,         8,    48,
  "rpmi_1e4",  "fAUC/MIC",  "stasis",   28,        19,    46,
  "rpmi_1e4",  "fAUC/MIC",  "EI50",     27,        18,    39,
  "rpmi_1e4",  "fAUC/MIC",  "EI10",     10,         5,    24,
  "rpmi_1e4",  "fAUC/MIC",  "EI5",       9,         3,    21,
  "rpmi_1e3",  "fAUC/MIC",  "stasis",   50,        42,    65,
  "rpmi_1e3",  "fAUC/MIC",  "EI50",     46,        38,    56,
  "rpmi_1e3",  "fAUC/MIC",  "EI10",     27,        18,    41,
  "rpmi_1e3",  "fAUC/MIC",  "EI5",      22,        13,    39
) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    simulated = invert_curve(thetas[[model]], target_change(thetas[[model]], endpoint))
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / reported - 1))

table1 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    simulated = signif(simulated, 3),
    pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1),
    ci = paste0(lo, "-", hi)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(model, index, endpoint, reported, ci, simulated, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Model" = model,
    "Index" = index,
    "Target" = endpoint,
    "Table 1" = reported,
    "Table 1 95% CI" = ci,
    "Packaged model" = simulated,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Packaged exposure-response curves vs Beredaki 2024 Table 1.")
```

```{r table-1-assert}
# Every recovered target must fall inside the paper's own 95% CI.
stopifnot(all(table1$simulated > table1$lo & table1$simulated < table1$hi))
# The serum curves use the published coefficients: every target within 5%.
serum_rows <- table1$model %in% c("serum_1e4", "serum_1e3")
stopifnot(max(abs(table1$pct_diff[serum_rows])) < 5)
# The digitised serum-free curves: stasis, EI10 and EI5 within 15%; EI50 is
# where Table 1 and the drawn curve disagree (see Assumptions and deviations).
rpmi_rows <- !serum_rows & table1$endpoint != "EI50"
stopifnot(max(abs(table1$pct_diff[rpmi_rows])) < 15)
```

The two serum curves, built from the published coefficients, reproduce all
eight Table 1 serum targets to within 3%. In particular the new target the paper
proposes -- EI10 at 10^3 CFU/mL -- comes out at
`r signif(table1$simulated[table1$model == "serum_1e3" & table1$endpoint == "EI10"], 3)`
tAUC0-24/MIC against the reported 28.

### The printed Hill coefficient of the 10^3 CFU/mL serum curve

Results print n = -1.15 for the 10^3 CFU/mL serum curve. The table below shows
what that value would give, holding the other published coefficients (Emin 5.23,
Emax -2, EI50 124) fixed, against the packaged n = 1.45.

```{r hill-check}
hill_check <- tibble::tibble(endpoint = c("stasis", "EI10", "EI5"), reported = c(240, 28, 16))
th_115 <- thetas$serum_1e3
th_115[["lhill"]] <- log(1.15)
hill_check$`n = 1.15 (as printed)` <- vapply(
  hill_check$endpoint,
  function(ep) invert_curve(th_115, target_change(th_115, ep)),
  numeric(1)
)
hill_check$`n = 1.45 (packaged)` <- vapply(
  hill_check$endpoint,
  function(ep) invert_curve(thetas$serum_1e3, target_change(thetas$serum_1e3, ep)),
  numeric(1)
)
hill_check |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Target" = endpoint, "Table 1 (tAUC0-24/MIC)" = reported) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Effect of the printed vs packaged Hill coefficient on the 10^3 CFU/mL serum targets.")

# The printed value misses EI10 and EI5 by more than a third; the packaged one
# reproduces all three to within 3%.
stopifnot(
  abs(hill_check$`n = 1.15 (as printed)`[2] / 28 - 1) > 0.3,
  max(abs(hill_check$`n = 1.45 (packaged)` / hill_check$reported - 1)) < 0.03
)
```

# Replicate Figures 2 and 3: time-kill curves

Figures 2 and 3 show the time-kill curves for each isolate and regimen in RPMI
and with 10% serum. The packaged models spread the fitted 72 h change uniformly
across the window, so each trajectory is a straight line on the log10 scale that
lands on the fitted endpoint at 72 h; the curvature within 72 h is not modelled.

```{r figures-2-3}
isolates <- tibble::tribble(
  ~isolate,          ~mic,
  "CP639 (MIC 2)",     2,
  "CP795 (MIC 1)",     1,
  "CP732 (MIC 0.5)", 0.5
)
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~medium,   ~cmax,
  "rpmi",      0,
  "rpmi",      0.5,
  "rpmi",      1.8,
  "rpmi",      4,
  "serum",     0,
  "serum",     2,
  "serum",     8,
  "serum",    32,
  "serum",    64
)
inocula <- tibble::tibble(inoculum = c("1e4", "1e3"))

tk_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(regimens, inocula, isolates) |>
  # CP732 did not grow in 10% serum, so it has no serum time-kill curve.
  dplyr::filter(!(medium == "serum" & mic == 0.5)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = paste0(medium, "_", inoculum))

timekill <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(tk_grid)), function(i) {
  g <- tk_grid[i, ]
  solve_arm(mods[[g$model]], cmax = g$cmax, mic = g$mic, dt = 4) |>
    dplyr::select(time, log10cfu, ei, change72) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      medium = g$medium, inoculum = g$inoculum, isolate = g$isolate, mic = g$mic,
      cmax = g$cmax,
      regimen = if (g$cmax == 0) {
        "drug-free control"
      } else {
        paste0(if (g$medium == "rpmi") "fCmax " else "tCmax ", g$cmax, " mg/L")
      }
    )
}))

timekill |>
  dplyr::filter(medium == "rpmi") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, log10cfu, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_grid(paste("inoculum", inoculum) ~ isolate) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 72, by = 24)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "log10 CFU/mL", colour = NULL,
    title = "Figure 2 -- in vitro time-kill in RPMI",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Beredaki 2024. Dotted line = limit of detection."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

timekill |>
  dplyr::filter(medium == "serum") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, log10cfu, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_grid(paste("inoculum", inoculum) ~ isolate) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 72, by = 24)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "log10 CFU/mL", colour = NULL,
    title = "Figure 3 -- in vitro time-kill in RPMI + 10% pooled human serum",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Beredaki 2024. Dotted line = limit of detection."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r timekill-endpoints}
endpoints <- timekill |>
  dplyr::group_by(medium, inoculum, isolate, mic, cmax, regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    change_72h = dplyr::last(log10cfu) - dplyr::first(log10cfu),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

endpoints |>
  dplyr::mutate(change_72h = round(change_72h, 2)) |>
  dplyr::select(medium, inoculum, isolate, regimen, change_72h) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = isolate, values_from = change_72h) |>
  dplyr::rename("Medium" = medium, "Inoculum" = inoculum, "Regimen" = regimen) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model 72 h change in log10 CFU/mL by medium, inoculum, regimen and isolate.")
```

```{r timekill-assert}
end_of <- function(med, ino, mic_val, cmax_val) {
  endpoints$change_72h[
    endpoints$medium == med & endpoints$inoculum == ino &
      endpoints$mic == mic_val & endpoints$cmax == cmax_val
  ]
}
# Results, "In RPMI": the initial log10 CFU/mL decreased for isolates with
# MIC <= 1 mg/L at fCmax 4 mg/L -- and not for CP639 (MIC 2). At 10^3 CFU/mL
# the CP795 arm (fAUC0-24/MIC about 40) lies below that curve's own stasis
# target of 50, so the fitted curve predicts growth there; see the text below.
stopifnot(end_of("rpmi", "1e4", 1, 4) < 0, end_of("rpmi", "1e4", 0.5, 4) < 0)
stopifnot(end_of("rpmi", "1e3", 0.5, 4) < 0)
stopifnot(end_of("rpmi", "1e4", 2, 4) > 0, end_of("rpmi", "1e3", 2, 4) > 0)
# Results, "In RPMI with 10% human serum": a fungicidal effect at tCmax 64 mg/L
# (2-2.8 log10 CFU/mL reduction) for both isolates at 10^4 CFU/mL.
stopifnot(end_of("serum", "1e4", 1, 64) < -2, end_of("serum", "1e4", 1, 64) > -2.8)
stopifnot(end_of("serum", "1e4", 2, 64) < -1.5)
# ... and a fungistatic effect at tCmax 32 mg/L against both isolates at
# 10^3 CFU/mL.
stopifnot(abs(end_of("serum", "1e3", 2, 32)) < 1, abs(end_of("serum", "1e3", 1, 32)) < 1)
# Drug-free controls reproduce each curve's zero-exposure change exactly.
ctrl <- endpoints |> dplyr::filter(cmax == 0)
ctrl_e0 <- vapply(paste0(ctrl$medium, "_", ctrl$inoculum), function(m) thetas[[m]][["e0"]], numeric(1))
stopifnot(max(abs(ctrl$change_72h - ctrl_e0)) < 1e-3)
```

The model reproduces most of the Results' threshold statements: killing in RPMI
at fCmax 4 mg/L for the MIC <= 1 mg/L isolates only (with one exception, below),
a 2-2.8 log10 reduction for
CP795 at tCmax 64 mg/L with serum (CP639 reaches
`r round(end_of("serum", "1e4", 2, 64), 2)`, slightly short of the reported
2 log10), and stasis at tCmax 32 mg/L with serum at the low inoculum.

The exception is CP795 at fCmax 4 mg/L with the 10^3 CFU/mL inoculum. Figure 2
shows that arm falling from about 2.5 to the limit of detection, but its
exposure under the reported 8 h half-life, an fAUC0-24/MIC of about
`r round(unique(timekill$ei[timekill$medium == "rpmi" & timekill$inoculum == "1e3" & timekill$mic == 1 & timekill$cmax == 4]), 1)`,
lies below the 10^3 CFU/mL curve's own Table 1 stasis target of 50, so the
published exposure-response predicts net growth
(`r round(end_of("rpmi", "1e3", 1, 4), 2)` log10 CFU/mL). The fitted curve is
steep there (n about 4.8), so a modest difference between the idealised and the
measured AUC of that experiment moves the prediction across stasis.

# Bridging to human data: probability of target attainment

Figure 5 carries the serum targets to patients by Monte Carlo simulation of
5000 patients given 100 mg micafungin IV q24h, whose total AUC0-24 is normal
with mean 97 and SD 29 mg*h/L. Because the distribution is normal and the
target is a threshold on tAUC0-24/MIC, the attainment probability is available
in closed form:

PTA(MIC, target) = P(tAUC0-24 >= target x MIC) = 1 - Phi((target x MIC - 97) / 29)

The targets are taken from the packaged serum curves (computed above).

```{r figure-5}
pta_targets <- table1 |>
  dplyr::filter(model %in% c("serum_1e4", "serum_1e3")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(inoculum = ifelse(model == "serum_1e4", "10^4 CFU/mL", "10^3 CFU/mL")) |>
  dplyr::select(inoculum, endpoint, target = simulated, reported)

mic_grid <- c(0.06, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
pta_of <- function(target, mic) {
  100 * stats::pnorm((target * mic - 97) / 29, lower.tail = FALSE)
}

pta_tbl <- tidyr::expand_grid(pta_targets, mic = mic_grid) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pta = pta_of(target, mic), pta_table1 = pta_of(reported, mic))

ggplot(pta_tbl, aes(factor(mic), pta, colour = endpoint, linetype = inoculum,
                    group = interaction(endpoint, inoculum))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 95, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "micafungin EUCAST/CLSI MIC (mg/L)", y = "Probability of target attainment (%)",
    colour = "PK/PD target", linetype = "Starting inoculum",
    title = "Figure 5 -- PTA for 100 mg micafungin q24h",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 5 of Beredaki 2024 analytically from the reported",
      "total AUC0-24 distribution (97 +/- 29 mg*h/L). Dotted line = 95% PTA."
    )
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r figure-5-table}
pta_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(mic %in% c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pta = round(pta, 1)) |>
  dplyr::select(inoculum, endpoint, mic, pta) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = mic, values_from = pta, names_prefix = "MIC ") |>
  dplyr::rename("Inoculum" = inoculum, "Target" = endpoint) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Analytic PTA (%) at selected MICs, using the packaged serum curves' targets.")
```

```{r figure-5-assert}
pta_at <- function(ino, ep, mic_val) {
  pta_tbl$pta[pta_tbl$inoculum == ino & pta_tbl$endpoint == ep & pta_tbl$mic == mic_val]
}
# The packaged targets and the Table 1 targets give the same PTA curves.
stopifnot(max(abs(pta_tbl$pta - pta_tbl$pta_table1)) < 5)
# Results: stasis PTA 86%, 10% and 0% at MICs 0.25, 0.5 and >= 1 mg/L for both
# inocula. The 10^3 stasis target (240) gives about 21% at 0.5 mg/L under the
# closed form whichever source supplies it, hence the looser bound there.
for (ino in c("10^4 CFU/mL", "10^3 CFU/mL")) {
  stopifnot(
    pta_at(ino, "stasis", 0.25) > 80, pta_at(ino, "stasis", 0.25) < 92,
    pta_at(ino, "stasis", 0.5) < 25,
    pta_at(ino, "stasis", 1) < 1
  )
}
stopifnot(pta_at("10^4 CFU/mL", "stasis", 0.5) < 15)
# Results: EI10 at 10^3 CFU/mL gives high PTA for susceptible isolates.
stopifnot(pta_at("10^3 CFU/mL", "EI10", 1) > 99, pta_at("10^3 CFU/mL", "EI10", 2) > 90)
```

The stasis-target PTAs reproduce the 86% / 10% / 0% the Results quote at MICs
of 0.25, 0.5 and >= 1 mg/L for the 10^4 CFU/mL inoculum. For 10^3 CFU/mL the
closed form gives
`r round(pta_at("10^3 CFU/mL", "stasis", 0.25), 1)`% and
`r round(pta_at("10^3 CFU/mL", "stasis", 0.5), 1)`% at 0.25 and 0.5 mg/L, and
the paper's own Table 1 stasis target (240) gives
`r round(pta_of(240, 0.5), 1)`% at 0.5 mg/L as well. For the proposed EI10 target at 10^3 CFU/mL the
analytic PTA at the breakpoint MIC of 2 mg/L is
`r round(pta_at("10^3 CFU/mL", "EI10", 2), 1)`%, a few points below the >= 95%
shown in Figure 5(c); the paper's own Table 1 value of 28 tAUC0-24/MIC gives
`r round(pta_of(28, 2), 1)`% under the same calculation, so the gap is in the
Monte Carlo procedure (not described beyond "the normal random number generator
function of Excel"), not in the packaged curve.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Four files, one per fitted curve.** Beredaki 2024 fitted the exposure-response
  separately for each medium and starting inoculum, and reports that the Emin
  and n of the two serum curves differ significantly (P = 0.04). Each fitted
  curve is therefore its own model file.
- **The printed Hill coefficient of the 10^3 CFU/mL serum curve is treated as a
  typesetting error.** Results print "the Emin (4 versus 5.23) and n (-2.9
  versus -1.15)". With Emin 5.23, the constrained Emax -2 and the published EI50
  124, n = 1.15 gives stasis, EI10 and EI5 of 286, 18 and 10 tAUC0-24/MIC
  against the Table 1 values 240, 28 and 16. n = 1.45 reproduces all three to
  within 3% (table above), and an independent least-squares trace of the drawn
  curve in Figure 4 gives n = 1.48 (with Emin 5.24 and EI50 126 tAUC0-24/MIC,
  confirming the other two published coefficients). The packaged model uses
  1.45. The 10^4 CFU/mL curve's printed coefficients (Emin 4, EI50 240, n 2.9)
  reproduce both Table 1 and the drawn curve and are used as published.
- **The serum-free exposure-response coefficients were digitised from Figure 4.**
  The paper prints Emin and n only for the serum curves. For the two RPMI curves
  the fitted lines in the right panel of Figure 4 were traced from the 200 dpi
  figure embedded in the publisher PDF, calibrated on the labelled decade ticks
  of the log10 x-axis and the y-axis ticks, and the published equation was
  least-squares fitted with Emax held at its constrained value (-3 or -2).
  Residual RMSE was 0.027 (10^4) and 0.037 (10^3) log10 CFU/mL. The recovered
  curves reproduce Table 1's stasis, EI10 and EI5 within 12%, but their EI50s
  (25.1 and 41.3 fAUC0-24/MIC) are 7% and 11% below Table 1's (27 and 46). No
  single curve with the drawn Emin can match all four Table 1 values -- with
  EI50 fixed at 46, the stasis and EI10 targets would require Emin of about 2.8
  for the 10^3 curve, against a plotted top asymptote of 4.4 and a control
  growth of 4.7 log10 CFU/mL -- so the drawn curve was taken as the authority.
- **Index scales.** The serum models are indexed on total AUC0-24/MIC, as in the
  paper's Methods and Table 1. The serum-free models are indexed on the AUC in
  the protein-free medium, which is fAUC0-24/MIC; Table 1's tAUC figures for
  RPMI are this value divided by 0.0025. Figure 4 plots both media on the fAUC
  axis.
- **`cmax` to AUC0-24 uses the idealised PK.** The model converts the target peak
  into the index analytically from the achieved mono-exponential half-life. The
  paper calculated each experiment's AUC0-24 from the measured profiles, which
  scatter around the targets (Figure 1). The exposure-response relationship --
  the part the paper fitted -- is unaffected, which is why the Table 1
  validation above is done on the index axis; time-kill endpoints at a given
  nominal Cmax can differ from Figures 2 and 3 by the scatter of the measured
  exposure.
- **`log10_cfu0` uses the measured rather than the nominal inoculum.** The mean
  t = 0 densities of the drug-free controls (4.28 / 3.2 with serum, 3.94 / 3.06
  in RPMI) are used so the simulated trajectories start where the figures do.
  Only the offset is affected; the model describes the change in log10 CFU/mL.
- **Linear 72 h trajectory.** Only the 72 h change was fitted, so the model
  spreads it uniformly over the window. The intermediate time points of
  Figures 2 and 3 (lag phases, early killing) are not described.
- **Residual error and variability.** The paper reports no assay CV and only R^2
  for the exposure-response fits, so `propSd` and `addSd_log10cfu` are fixed at
  0 and the models are for deterministic typical-value simulation. The in vitro
  experiment has no hierarchical structure and no eta parameters.
- **The PTA replication is analytic, not Monte Carlo.** The paper drew 5000
  patients from a normal total-AUC0-24 distribution in Excel; the closed form is
  used so the vignette is deterministic.
- **Not packaged.** The pan-echinocandin-resistant isolate (no effect at any
  exposure) and the static serum-growth screen of 20 isolates have no fitted
  model in the paper.
